claims.text: A thin Cu interlayer in HEA multilayers will facilitate a transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
A Cu interlayer will modify interface coherency in HEA multilayers.
A Cu interlayer will modify local diffusion properties in HEA multilayers.
As-fabricated HEA multilayer interfaces span coherent, semi-coherent, and incoherent states.
High-temperature, low-to-moderate-stress conditions permit both atomic diffusion and dislocation movement to contribute to creep.
Cu has diffusivity suitable for changing atomic mobility at HEA multilayer interfaces.
A Cu interlayer will create interfaces with intermediate coherency.
Interfaces created by the Cu interlayer will mediate atomic mobility.
Interfaces created by the Cu interlayer will mediate dislocation nucleation.
Relatively fast atomic mobility in the Cu layer will enhance diffusion creep at lower stresses.
The Cu layer will provide a source for slip and dislocation nucleation as stress increases.
The combination of enhanced diffusion and dislocation nucleation will produce a regime in which diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep coexist.
Cu-containing HEA multilayers will exhibit a measurable shift in creep behavior relative to multilayers without Cu interlayers.
Cu-containing HEA multilayers will transition from predominantly diffusion-controlled creep at lower stresses to dislocation-mediated creep at higher stresses.
Baseline multilayers with coherent interfaces are expected to be governed predominantly by fast diffusion.
Baseline multilayers with incoherent interfaces are expected to be governed predominantly by dislocation dynamics.
The Cu-interlayer effect will be significant only within a temperature and stress regime where both creep mechanisms are active.
The influence of the Cu interlayer may be minimal at very low temperatures or extremely high stresses.
